chunks: And it is narrated from Muḥammad al-Ṭayyār, who said:

I entered al-Madīnah and looked for a house to rent. Then I entered a dwelling in which there were two rooms with a door between them, and in it was a woman. She said, "Will you rent this room?" I said, "There is a door between them, and I am a young man." She said, "I will close the door between me and you." So I moved my belongings into it and said to her, "Close the door." She said, "The air comes to me through it; leave it." So I said, "No, I am a young man and you are a young woman; close it." She said, "Sit in your room; I will not come to you nor approach you," but she refused to close it.
So I went to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and asked him about that, and he said: "Move out from it, for when a man and a woman are left alone in a house, the third of them is al-Shayṭān."

key_terms.الشَّيْطَانَ: Satan, indicating the spiritual danger present in such seclusion
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةَ: al-Madīnah, the city where the incident took place
key_terms.امْرَأَةٌ: a woman residing in the dwelling
key_terms.بَيْتًا: a room or house sought for lodging
key_terms.تَحَوَّلْ: move away or relocate from that place
key_terms.خُلِّيَا: were left alone together in seclusion
key_terms.شَابٌّ: a young man, indicating potential vulnerability to temptation
key_terms.شَابَّةٌ: a young woman, likewise indicating youth

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about a man and woman being alone together in one house?
ai.summary: This hadith relates an incident in which Muḥammad al-Ṭayyār sought guidance from Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام regarding lodging in close seclusion with a young woman. The Imam عليه السلام instructed him to leave, establishing the danger and impropriety of khalwah between an unrelated man and woman.
